readiness: No blocker or major item is open. 4 minor items to settle.

findings.title: The port capacitors and safe-idle pull resistors are drawn away from the connectors they serve, joined only by net labels.
findings.what: The 6 port capacitors C51 and C53-C57 (1 uF on six ASIC rails) and the 18 pull resistors R2-R6 and R16-R28, which hold the ASIC control lines at a safe level, each reach their net only through a 5 to 10 mm wire stub and a net label. The other pin has a power symbol or a shared ground or label stub. None is wired to a J1-J4 pin or to a local bus there: the capacitors sit at x 345 to 406 and the pulls at x 403 to 715, while J1/J2 are at x 74.93 and J3/J4 at x 270.51. The C51 note box itself says C51, C53, C55 and C57 sit at the J3/J4 ports. The netlist is correct: ERC (KiCad's schematic rule check) reports 0 errors, and the schematic-to-layout check finds 0 differences. The project's drawing rule asks for support parts to be wired visibly to the pins they serve and kept beside that circuit.
findings.consequence: No electrical effect. A reader at a connector cannot see which pins are pulled up, pulled down or decoupled, so checking the safe-idle levels against the pin map is slow and error-prone.
findings.do: In the next schematic revision, redraw the pull resistors beside the J1-J4 pins they serve and the port capacitors beside J3/J4, with continuous wires to those pins or a short local bus, keeping their note boxes beside them. Keep the netlist identical and rerun ERC and DRC with schematic parity.
findings.source: FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V24.kicad_sch: wires, labels and symbol positions; exported netlist ; workspace rule 'Visible schematic connections'

findings.title: Correct turning of U1, the bottom regulators and the two diodes depends on JLC's placement check, and U3 has no pin-1 mark.
findings.what: 76 of the 82 parts placed on the board are on the bottom. The placement file gives KiCad's own bottom-side angles; the assembly remark asks JLC to place every polarised part by the pin-1 table and to confirm placement before production, and the order waits for that confirmation. JLC has not yet shown a detailed placement preview. On the silkscreen U3 (1 x 1 mm X2SON) has no pin-1 dot, and the dots of U4 and U5 sit 0.75 to 0.86 mm from pad 2 and 1.4 to 1.5 mm from pad 1.
findings.consequence: A half-turned U1 puts its GND pin 13 on the VIN_3V3 pad and shorts the stack's 3.3 V; a reversed D12 drives the -12 V node positive; a turned X2SON regulator is found only at power-up.
findings.do: In JLC's placement confirmation, check pin 1 of U1 to U10 and the cathodes of D11 and D12 against the pin-1 table and drawings before approving. When the silkscreen is next edited, add a dot for U3 and move the U4/U5 dots to the pad-1 end.
findings.source: order_frame_V4/FPGA_LDO_A_V24_Test_Frame_V4_CPL_JLC.csv, FPGA_LDO_A_V24_Test_Frame_V4_Pin1_Table.csv, order_frame_V4/JLC_Remarks_paste.txt ; FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V24.kicad_pcb: B.Silkscreen ; LT3582 data sheet p.8 pin functions https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/3582512fb.pdf

findings.title: The DF40 board-to-board connectors get full-size solder-paste openings, and the order does not set the top-side stencil thickness.
findings.what: J1, J2 and J3 (top) and J4 (bottom) are Hirose DF40 connectors at 0.4 mm pitch. No paste reduction is set on the board, the footprints or the pads, so every paste opening is the full pad: 0.23 x 0.66 mm on the top plugs (0.17 mm between pads) and 0.20 x 0.70 mm on J4, as the order Gerbers confirm. The assembly remark asks for a 0.10 mm stencil on the bottom only and says nothing about the top, where J1-J3 are three of the six parts. Hirose recommends a 0.12 mm stencil with 80 % openings for DF40 and allows at most two reflow cycles.
findings.consequence: If JLC uses a 0.12 mm top stencil and does not shrink the openings itself, J1-J3 get about 125 % of Hirose's paste volume. That raises the chance of solder bridges between pads, which are hard to see once the connector is soldered. J4 at 0.10 mm with full openings is about equal to Hirose's figure. In this two-sided build the connector on the side soldered first already goes through two reflows, so reflow rework of that connector would exceed Hirose's limit.
findings.do: In the assembly remark, ask for a 0.10 mm stencil on both sides, or reduce the DF40 paste openings to about 80 % in the footprints and regenerate the paste Gerbers. Ask JLC not to rework DF40 joints by reflow.
findings.source: FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V24.kicad_pcb: DF40 footprints (no paste margin) ; order_frame_V4/FPGA_LDO_A_V24_Test_Frame_V4_gerbers.zip (F_Paste, B_Paste) ; order_frame_V4/JLC_Remarks_paste.txt ; Hirose DF40 catalogue p.21 (stencil 0.12 mm, 80 % opening, 2 reflow cycles max) https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40

findings.title: Some schematic fields and note boxes are out of date, incomplete or understate the ordered parts.
findings.what: Fields: the Mating fields of J3 and J4 name 'ASIC bottom board V6' (the mating boards are ASIC V15), and those of J1 and J2 say 'pin map V6' (pin map V8 differs from V6 at J1.36 and J2.48, the two bottom-board latch contacts). Title-block comment 3 says 'Pin map V6', while comment 1 names pin map V8. The Datasheet link of J1-J4 points to the DF40 series catalogue but ends in productCode=C3640153, the JLC number of a different part (a 10-contact DF40GB receptacle), and J1-J4 have no 'Datasheet rev'. The 'Datasheet rev' field is empty on the LT3042s (U2, U6, U8, U9) and the LT3094 (U10), and the LT3042 MPN (manufacturer part number) reads LT3042EDD#PBF while the ordered JLC part C580010 is the reel version LT3042EDD#TRPBF. The Voltage fields of C1 (10 V) and C2 (16 V) understate the ordered parts (C602037, 25 V; C307331, 50 V). 27 resistors and capacitors carry a JLC number but no MPN, and the Datasheet field is empty on all 39 capacitors and on 15 resistors. JP1 and JP2, bare-copper solder jumpers, are set to go in the BOM with no JLC number, unlike NT1 and the test pads: the order BOM leaves them out, but a BOM exported from KiCad gets a line for the two jumpers with no C-number. Notes: the J1/J2 connector box says the Frontend has not adopted pin map V6 yet, and the 5 V box says the Frontend does not drive J1.32 yet (Frontend 14 layers V13 follows pin map V8 and puts VIN_5V on J1.32). The port-capacitor box says the ASIC board capacitor values are not yet given (the ASIC boards V15 carry 10 nF + 100 nF per rail pair plus C63). The VIN_3V3 box marks the LT3042 enable threshold 'to confirm', though the data sheet gives 1.18 to 1.32 V (1.24 V typical) and the schematic's own regulator box already says about 1.24 V. The safe-idle box cites '(AMD UG470, PUDC_B)' with no revision, page or URL.
findings.consequence: Anyone reading the schematic, or rebuilding a BOM from it, sees the wrong mating revisions and ratings, a wrong part tag on the connector data sheet and open questions that are already settled, and a BOM exported from KiCad carries a line JLC cannot match. No electrical effect.
findings.do: In the next schematic revision: set the J1-J4 Mating fields to pin map V8 and ASIC V15, and comment 3 to pin map V8; link J1-J4 to the Hirose DF40 catalogue with its date; fill the empty Datasheet, 'Datasheet rev' and MPN fields, matching the LT3042 MPN to C580010; correct the C1/C2 Voltage fields; set Exclude from BOM on JP1 and JP2, as on NT1 and the test pads; rewrite the four stale note sentences and give UG470 its revision, PUDC_B page and URL. No copper change.

findings.title: The DC-bias loss of the ceramic capacitors on the +/-12 V and +/-8 V stimulation rails has not been checked against the regulator minimums.
findings.what: The LT3094 needs at least 10 uF on its output and 10 uF on its input; the LT3042 needs 4.7 uF on each. U10 has C1002 (22 uF 1206) and C1004 (10 uF 0805) at -8 V, and one local 10 uF 0805 input capacitor, C1001, at -12 V (C21, 22 uF 0805, is on the same net through JP2). U9 has C902 (22 uF 1206) at +8 V and C901 (10 uF 0805) at +12 V (C14 through JP1). C14 and C21 are also U1's +/-12 V output capacitors, and the LT3582 data sheet warns that small 0805 and 0603 ceramics keep much less than their marked value at the working voltage. All are 25 V X5R parts whose product pages give no DC-bias curve.
findings.consequence: If the effective capacitance falls below a minimum, a +/-8 V rail can ring, and low effective capacitance at C14/C21 raises the converter's +/-12 V ripple. Ringing is unlikely on the outputs; the single 10 uF input capacitors at 12 V are closest to the limit.
findings.do: Get the maker's DC-bias data for CL21A106KAYNNNE, CL31A226KAHNNNE and CL21A226MAYNNNE (C14/C21) at 8 to 12 V, or measure. If C1001 keeps less than about 6 uF, fit 22 uF 1206 (C12891) at C1001 and C901.
findings.source: LT3094 data sheet Rev 0 p.20 'Stability and Input Capacitance' https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/lt3094.pdf ; LT3042 data sheet Rev A p.16-17 https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/lt3042.pdf ; LT3582 data sheet Rev B p.19 (capacitor selection) https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/3582512fb.pdf ; https://product.samsungsem.com/mlcc/CL21A106KAYNNN.do ; FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V24.kicad_pcb

findings.title: Switching noise from the LT3582 on the stimulation rails and near REF_VCM must be measured.
findings.what: U1 has no fixed frequency: about 50 kHz at light load, rising with load. Each ASIC channel samples at 31.25 kS/s, so ripple that reaches it folds into the recording band as a tone that moves with load. U10 (LT3094, ASIC_VSS10) rejects only about 25 to 35 dB near 10 MHz. The boost switch node SW_P runs 1.98 mm from U8's SET trace on the bottom layer. The L3/L4 ground planes have no cuts around the converter, and U1's exposed pad has two vias, where data sheet Figure 12 shows cut islands and more pad vias.
findings.consequence: Possible tones or spurs on ASIC_VDD10, ASIC_VSS10 and REF_VCM that reach the recordings. The size is not known.
findings.do: At bring-up, record ASIC shorted-input spectra with U1 running, and again with JP1/JP2 cut and a bench supply on TP8/TP9. Measure VSS10, VDD10 and REF_VCM at J4 with a 20 MHz-limited probe and a short ground spring.
findings.source: LT3582 data sheet Rev B p.6 (frequency vs load), p.21 and Figure 12 (layout) https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/3582512fb.pdf ; LT3094 data sheet Rev 0 p.11-12 (PSRR) https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/lt3094.pdf ; FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V24.kicad_pcb

findings.title: The top-layer lanes use the L2 analog-ground plane as their return path, some clock lanes have no plane under them, and one data lane runs beside the REF_VDD pour.
findings.what: L2 is the AGND plane, 0.071 mm under L1. About 277 mm of the 645 mm of top-layer signal lanes run over it, so their return current flows in AGND, which meets GND only at NT1. Where AGND is absent, the nearest plane is L3 GND, about 0.3 mm down. These lanes have no AGND under them: ASIC8_CLK32MHz_Out for all 9.2 mm, ASIC7_CLK32MHz_Out for 6.0 of 15.1 mm, ASIC5_CLK32MHz_Out for 7.2 of 19.7 mm, and ASIC7_8_TOP_SPI_CLK for 10.3 of 10.7 mm. On L1, ASIC7_DATA6 (0.1 mm wide) runs from J3 pin 58 at (103.18, 114.87) straight to (103.18, 127.5), and for 10.1 mm of that it lies 0.20 to 0.25 mm from the edge of the L1 REF_VDD pour. C55 (1 uF on REF_VDD, bottom) sits beside the middle of that run, about 1.2 mm away, so that point is well bypassed.
findings.consequence: Lane edges may put noise on AGND beside the reference regulators U2, U6 and U8 and between the ASIC's AGND and DGND pins, and ASIC7's data edges may couple into REF_VDD. Clocks over the gaps see an impedance step and more crosstalk. The size is not known.
findings.do: On a first board, measure AGND to GND at J4 (pins 42/44 to 46/48) and the noise on REF_VCM and REF_VDD while the lanes run, compare REF_VDD and recording noise with ASIC7 idle and streaming, and check the ASIC5, ASIC7 and ASIC8 clocks at the FPGA.
findings.where: L1 lanes over the L2_AGND_PLANE fill; ASIC7_DATA6 on L1 at x 103.18, y 114.87 to 127.5, beside the L1_PWR_ASIC_REF_VDD pour; C55 bottom (102.0, 122.7); NT1 bottom (100.58, 121.0); U2 (98.85, 135.6), U6 (104.5, 135.6), U8 (93.2, 135.6).
findings.source: FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V24.kicad_pcb: refilled L2_AGND_PLANE and L1 tracks, sampled every 0.05 mm, and the L1 REF_VDD pour edge against ASIC7_DATA6 ; stack-up JLCH061611Y1-1078 (L1-L2 0.071 mm, L2-L3 0.201 mm)

findings.title: The converter's pulsed return current crosses the single AGND-GND tie NT1, and several regulator grounds reach their plane through traces.
findings.what: VIN_3V3 capacitors C201, C301, C401, C601, C701, C801 and the stimulation-regulator input capacitors C901 and C1001 return to AGND, so part of the LT3582's switching current goes back to GND through NT1. The tie runs from the ASIC's AGND pins J4.42/44 to its DGND pins J4.46/48 through four 0.2 mm bottom-layer traces of about 5 to 6 mm, roughly 15 mOhm, so the tie voltage appears directly between the ASIC's two grounds. U4 and C53 also return partly along this tie trace. The set networks R901/C903 (U9) and R1001/C1003 (U10) are 2.4 to 3.7 mm of trace from the nearest AGND via, C902, C1002 and C1004 2.8 to 4.0 mm, and U5's GND pins 1.7 to 2.1 mm.
findings.consequence: Converter ripple, estimated at about 1 mV rms but not measured, may sit between the ASIC's AGND and DGND and on VDD10, VSS10 and VDD_DRIVER. Its effect on recordings depends on the ASIC's supply and ground rejection, which is not documented.
findings.do: On a first board with U1 running, measure J4.44 to J4.46 and the ripple on ASIC_VDD10, ASIC_VSS10 and ASIC_VDD_DRIVER at J4.
findings.source: FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V24.kicad_pcb: NT1, L6 AGND/GND tracks and vias ; FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V24.kicad_sch: capacitor ground nets

findings.title: Noise margin on the CLK32 clock lanes and the stimulation control lines must be measured on a first board.
findings.what: Each port's ASIC outputs return through J3/J4 pins 3, 5, 46, 48 (GND) and 42, 44 (AGND), and on the Frontend side through the 15 J1/J2 ground pins, 13 of which have their own via at or near the pad. On the bottom layer, ASIC1_CLK32MHz_Out runs 8.7 mm at a 0.10 mm gap between ASIC1_DATA5 and ASIC1_SYNC, and STIM_CLK_SHARED runs 8.0 mm between STIM_EN_SHARED and STIM_START_SHARED; STIM_EN_SHARED also runs 8.2 mm beside ASIC1_SYNC. Top-layer lanes lie directly over other nets' L2 lanes for about 147 mm in all, the longest ASIC7_DATA6 over STIM_CHIP3_SPI_DR (8.8 mm); ASIC7_CLK32MHz_Out lies 1.7 mm over ASIC3_4_TOP_SPI_LATCH and 0.7 mm over ASIC3_SPI_DL. The ASIC inputs are 1.5 V Schmitt triggers and its edges are about 1 ns or slower, but no threshold or drive figures are given.
findings.consequence: Ground bounce plus crosstalk could cause bit slips on a CLK32 lane, or a false STIM_START or STIM_CLK edge at the ASIC. Neither is simulated for the current copper.
findings.do: On a first board, probe CLK32 at the FPGA with all ASICs sending data, and STIM_START_SHARED, STIM_EN_SHARED and STIM_CLK_SHARED at J4 while the lanes toggle. If margins are thin, widen the bottom-layer gaps to 0.3 mm or add series resistors at the ASIC outputs.
findings.where: L6: ASIC1_CLK32MHz_Out from the J4.45 via near (109.69, 115.15) along y 113.36; STIM_CLK/EN/START_SHARED alongside. L1 over L2: ASIC7_DATA6 / STIM_CHIP3_SPI_DR, ASIC7_CLK32MHz_Out / ASIC3_4_TOP_SPI_LATCH and ASIC3_SPI_DL.
findings.source: FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V24.kicad_pcb: L1/L2/L6 tracks, gaps sampled every 0.05 mm ; AMD DS181 Table 8 (LVCMOS15 levels) https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ds181_Artix_7_Data_Sheet

findings.title: The board's DRC setup leaves the mask-web and silkscreen-clearance limits at 0 and ignores seven check types, so DRC would not flag some later mistakes.
findings.what: DRC is KiCad's layout rule check. The minimum solder-mask web is set to 0 mm. The smallest mask web on the board lies between 0.16 and 0.18 mm (DRC at 0.16 mm is clean, at 0.18 mm it reports 199 bridges at the DF40 pads), above JLC's 0.10 mm green limit. The minimum silkscreen clearance is also 0, and the project ignores seven check types: footprint library mismatch and library issues, footprint filter and type mismatch, missing courtyard, track not centred on a via, and tuning-profile geometry. With those set to warning and a 0.15 mm silkscreen clearance, DRC reports 89 more items, all harmless today. 64 are footprint mismatches in which the pads match the project library; on the DFN and X2SON regulators the only pad difference is the bottom-side mirroring. 14 are track ends 0.002 to 0.15 mm off a via centre but inside the via pad. 8 are silkscreen items closer than 0.15 mm: seven where the pin-1 dots of U2, U4, U6 and U8 sit 0.128 to 0.135 mm from part outlines, and one where the 'NT1' text is 0.143 mm from the 'A' label. The last 3 are on J2, whose pin-1 silk triangle comes within 0.09 mm of the board edge.
findings.consequence: Edge routing may clip part of J2's pin-1 triangle, which marks the connector's orientation. Otherwise no effect on the current files, but a mask sliver, footprint drift or off-centre track added by a later edit would pass DRC.
findings.do: Set the minimum mask web to 0.10 mm (DRC stays clean at that value) and the minimum silkscreen clearance to 0.15 mm in the board setup, move J2's pin-1 triangle at least 0.15 mm in from the edge, and turn the footprint-mismatch and via-centring checks back on as warnings.
findings.where: Board setup: solder mask minimum web, minimum silkscreen clearance, rule severities. Top: J2 pin-1 silk triangle at x 110.71 to 111.23, y 119.91 to 120.49, against the east edge at x 111.32. Bottom: pin-1 dots of U2, U4, U6, U8.
findings.source: FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V24.kicad_pcb and .kicad_pro: board setup and rule severities ; DRC runs on copies with the ignored checks set to warning ; JLCPCB capabilities, solder mask bridge 0.10 mm (green) https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities

findings.title: U7's thermal pad has a laser via at its centre, which TI's data sheet advises against for this tiny package.
findings.what: A 0.10 mm L5-L6 laser via (0.26 mm pad, AGND) sits at the centre of pad 5, the 0.58 mm thermal pad of U7, inside its paste opening. U7 is the 1 x 1 mm TPS7A2015 that makes VDD_CGEN. U3, U4 and U5 have no via in this pad. TI says not to put a via directly under the thermal pad of this package, because it can wick solder away. Its land-pattern notes allow a via that is filled, plugged or tented. The PCB remark asks for copper-filled, planarised laser vias and for pads with vias in them to come out flat and solderable, which meets that note if it is applied to this via.
findings.consequence: If the via is left dimpled, the small paste deposit on U7's pad can be drawn into it, leaving U7, the VDD_CGEN regulator, weakly soldered or tilted. The risk is low with copper fill.
findings.do: At JLC's file review, confirm that the copper-filled, planarised laser vias include the one in U7's pad. In a later layout, move the via off the pad as on U3, U4 and U5.
findings.source: FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V24.kicad_pcb: U7 pad 5 and vias ; order_frame_V4/JLC_Remarks_paste.txt (via treatment) ; TPS7A20 data sheet SBVS338H section 7.4.1 and land-pattern note 8 https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps7a20.pdf

findings.title: Copper is spread unevenly between the layers (L2 70 %, L5 17 %), and the order remark forbids adding balancing copper inside the board.
findings.what: Measured on the refilled board, copper covers L1 41 %, L2 70 %, L3 90 %, L4 90 %, L5 17 % and L6 53 % of the board area. L2 (the AGND plane) and L5 (lanes only, no pour) are mirror layers about the 0.83 mm core of the JLCH061611Y1-1078 stack-up. L5 sits on the 0.071 mm prepreg that the 106 L5-L6 laser vias pass through. The PCB remark says balancing copper elsewhere on the frame is fine but asks JLC to add none inside the board outline.
findings.consequence: A thinly coppered L5 opposite a nearly full L2 raises the risk of bow and twist. It can also change the pressed thickness of the 0.071 mm L5-L6 dielectric, which sets the laser-via depth. On a 22.6 x 36.8 mm board the effect is probably small, and JLC may raise it at its file check.
findings.do: At JLC's production-file confirmation, ask whether 17 % copper on L5 is acceptable for this stack-up. If JLC wants balancing copper, allow a non-functional hatch on L5 only, at least 0.5 mm from lanes, or accept JLC's own proposal.
findings.where: L2 (L2_AGND_PLANE) and L5 (L5_SIG_RAILS) across the whole 22.64 x 36.76 mm board; order_frame_V4/JLC_Remarks_paste.txt (PCB remark).
findings.source: FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V24.kicad_pcb: refilled zones, tracks and stack-up ; order_frame_V4/JLC_Remarks_paste.txt (PCB remark)

findings.title: The 3D models of the two inductors and the four tiny regulators do not match the fitted parts, so the 3D stack files show them wrongly.
findings.what: L11 and L12 use a 1.0 mm-tall Murata DFE201610P model, but the fitted TDK VLS201612HBX-6R8M-1 is up to 1.2 mm tall. U3, U4, U5 and U7 (1 x 1 mm X2SON packages, about 0.4 mm tall) have only a hand-made VRML model, which KiCad's STEP (3D CAD file) export skips, so they are missing from the STEP files and print models. U1's model has a 1.7 mm exposed pad against the footprint's 1.45 mm; only the underside differs, its 0.785 mm height fits the LT3582's 0.80 mm maximum, and KiCad 10 does not install the matching 1.45 mm model, so it is a reasonable stand-in.
findings.consequence: The 3D views and the stack print models show L11/L12 0.2 mm too low and leave out the four regulators. None of these parts lies under the ASIC stacks (which end at y 117.1), so no collision is hidden today.
findings.do: When the models are next touched, give L11/L12 a 1.2 mm model (or scale the existing one) and add a STEP box for the X2SON parts so they export. U1 can keep its model.
findings.source: FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V24.kicad_pcb: footprint 3D model links ; JLC part page for L11/L12 (TDK VLS201612HBX-6R8M-1, 2.0 x 1.6 x 1.2 mm) https://jlcpcb.com/partdetail/C501945 ; LT3582 data sheet package drawing https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/3582512fb.pdf

findings.title: The +12 V test pad TP2 is 0.6 mm from the enable pad TP4.
findings.what: TP2 (STIM_POS_12V) and TP4 (EN_ASIC_RAILS) are 1.0 mm pads at 1.6 mm pitch, a 0.6 mm gap; TP5 (GND) is equally close on the other side. EN_ASIC_RAILS drives U1's SHDN pin (absolute maximum 6 V) and the enable pins of U3, U4, U5 and U7 (6.5 V). The Frontend does not cover these pads, so they are probed on a powered stack.
findings.consequence: A probe slip bridging TP2 and TP4 puts about 12 V on these enable pins and can destroy U1 and the four TPS7A20 regulators, which sit on the bottom side.
findings.do: Probe TP2 only with a fine spring tip, never a clip lead. In a later layout, move TP2 at least 2 mm from TP4.
findings.source: FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V24.kicad_pcb: TP1, TP2, TP4, TP5 ; LT3582 data sheet p.2 (SHDN 6 V max) https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/3582512fb.pdf ; TPS7A20 data sheet SBVS338H section 5.1 (EN 6.5 V max) https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps7a20.pdf
